newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Talk of a market top emerging.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Talk of a market top emerging.

text.p: U.S. stocks continued their choppy ways Thursday, keeping major index option volatilities pumped up, and talk of a market top was beginning to emerge.
By about 1245 CDT/1745 GMT, the Dow industrial average .DJI was down 41 points at 7,649. The average had traded in a 100-point range.
On Wednesday, the blue chip measure lost 68 points after rallying 75.
It slumped 192 points Monday only to recover 154 Tuesday.

Christopher Cadbury, who publishes a daily market letter, said equity put/call ratios at the Chicago Board Options Exchange and American Stock Exchange have recently reached what he called market-topping levels.
"About three times as many calls were trading as puts on equities," he said, adding that the ratio remained high through much of Wednesday's session before the market reversed course and headed down.
At the CBOE, equity call volume was 177,386 compared to put volume of 84,957 in early afternoon despite the market's selloff.
Among index options, put volume held a narrow lead over call volume. Puts led calls by 20,947 to 14,970 in the S&P 100 index .OEX and by 17,652 to 12,893 in the S&P 500 .SPX.
"Most (market) tops are made over a period of time," Cadbury said. "You go into a trading range and then you come down.
"So I would expect the market to flatten out here and even perhaps rally a bit before it goes lower," he added.
Any rally would likely fail at the highs, with 7,800 on the Dow the key level.
Cadbury noted that the Dow penetrated 7,800 three times last week but failed to close above that level and repeated the pattern Wednesday.

Timothy Ord, publisher of the daily Ord Oracle, said his analysis of a candlestick chart of September S&P 500 futures indicated a short-term top or consolidation was in place but that longer term the market remained in good shape.
"We've probably hit a month-long consolidation at least, with support at 870 and resistance at 910," he said.
Thursday afternoon, September S&P 500 futures were up 1.45 at 897.70 after dropping to 890.50 intraday.
He said a trendline connecting the February 19 and May 27 highs comes into play around 873.
"Until we break that line at 873 decisively, I think we're just in a trading range," Ord said.
